$AMD is nearing its $NVDA moment..

Digitimes saw data center AI chip shipments at 53 million units in 2030.

They estimated that 10% of this would be data center CPUs, 13% would be networking processors. This comes up to roughly 8:1 GPU-to-CPU ratio.

If this balance shifts to 2:1 due to agentic AI, we'll need to ship 15 million more CPUs in 2030.

At an average price of $10,000, we are looking at an additional $150 billion in CPU revenue in 2030.

Assuming 75%-25% mix of x86 and $ARM, and 40% revenue share for $AMD in the x86 segment, $AMD will generate $45 billion in revenue from data center CPUs in 2030.

For reference, its full-year revenue last year was just $35 billion.

Couldn't be more bullish on $AMD.

parse.keyClaim: AMD could generate $45 billion in revenue from data center CPUs in 2030 due to a potential shift in GPU-to-CPU ratio driven by agentic AI, representing ~29% upside vs. 2025 total revenue of $35 billion.
